survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This document is an assessment framework for PIRLS 2011 and does not report an empirical student-level analysis. As a result, it does not specify whether complex survey weights (e.g., student sampling weights) or replicate-weight procedures (e.g., BRR/jackknife) were applied. For analysts using PIRLS 2011 microdata, weighting should follow the PIRLS/TIMSS international database documentation for the relevant sampling design (school and student selection) and should be applied when producing population-representative estimates. Plausible values and scaling for PIRLS reading achievement are part of the assessment design described in the framework, but this framework text excerpt does not provide the PV or missing-data operational details.

data.outcome_summary: This PIRLS 2011 Assessment Framework document explains how PIRLS reading is conceptualized and operationalized for the 2011 cycle, including the reading purposes and processes of reading comprehension, the contexts for learning to read, and the assessment design and specifications. It is not an empirical paper that estimates model effects or trains predictive algorithms on PIRLS microdata; therefore, it does not report performance metrics, target variables, or benchmark comparisons. The framework is intended to guide instrument construction (e.g., what is measured and how), and it supports later analyses by clarifying the constructs and design choices underlying PIRLS reading achievement. In the provided text excerpt, no sampling design, student sample sizes, plausible-value generation/combining rules, or missing-data procedures are specified for an analytic dataset.
